gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: Had I realized the danger, I ___ the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Had I realized …' = 'If I had realized …' + would have cancelled.

gaps.sentence: As long as the budget ___, we can hire two more staff.
gaps.hint: as long as plus a passive condition
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is approved.

gaps.sentence: If you had set an alarm, you ___.
gaps.explanation: The present result of a past unreal condition takes 'would not be': would not still be asleep.

gaps.sentence: If the route ___ safer, I would cycle to work.
gaps.hint: an imaginary present situation, subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: Unreal present conditions formally take 'were' rather than 'is': were.

gaps.sentence: You'd have got a better exchange rate ___ at the bank instead of the airport.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes 'if + past perfect'.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.
